content:
Levi's Picked a Specialist Over the Platform That Sells Itself to Everyone

In this issue

  • Scaling up in America. The story has shifted since I last wrote about SCAYLE.
  • Where the everyone-for-everyone pitch runs out. Shopify has spent years marketing a strong argument that one platform can carry a merchant from a first sale through a global enterprise rollout, and for an enormous number of brands that argument is correct, which is a large part of why the company holds the position it holds.
  • The agentic story. The homepage says agentic commerce ready architecture. but ready is not shipped.
  • Strengths. DEICHMANN is the delivery proof, a European footwear leader turning 8.1 billion euros across 31 countries and 41 online shops, which decided on SCAYLE in late 2022 and had the Czech and Slovak shops live on May 31 2023, six months from project start.
  • Who it is for, and who it is not for. For high-volume consumer and fashion brands that want proven execution today, that value a unified engine over an assembly project, and that are comfortable building their own agent layer when the moment arrives, SCAYLE will meet the requirements.
  • The readiness score, and what it means here. My readiness score, and this one is scored on paper.
